corpus_gaps: The Partition Law (No. 21 of 1977) is not in the corpus, so the conclusiveness of the Final Decree of 22 October 2001 in District Court Kaduwela Case No 2525/P as a root of title cannot be supported from a provision.

No provision in the corpus governs the creation, reservation or termination of a life interest reserved by a donor in a deed of gift, or the effect of an absolute and irrevocable donation of immovable property. Section 36 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance remits such questions to Roman-Dutch common law, which is not in the corpus.

The corpus has no provision creating a presumption of intestacy where a deceased is described only as having died, with no mention of a will. The shares computed for Anusha and Prema assume each died intestate.

Sections 25 to 31 are the only material in the corpus on ascendants and collaterals, so the exception in section 29 for a surviving ascendant on the intestate's other side could not be tested against any further authority.

Verifier: no corpus provision creates a presumption that a person described only as having died left no will, so applying Part III to Anusha's and Prema's estates rests on an assumption stated in the Q02 answer, not on authority.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The intestacy links in the chain are fully statutory (Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance Part III), but a complete pedigree of title must also state the effect of the two non-statutory links: the vesting of Lot 1 in Mahesh under the Final Decree in Partition Case No 2525/P, and the operation of Deed of Gift No 925 as an absolute and irrevocable gift subject to a reserved life interest that fell in on the donor's death in 2008. The Partition Law is not in this corpus, and the corpus contains no provision governing the creation or termination of a life interest reserved by a donor; section 36 of the Ordinance itself remits such silences to Roman-Dutch common law, which is outside the corpus.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Whether a complete pedigree of the devolution of title to Lot 1 from Mahesh Gunesekara to the present owners can be drawn on the statutory material available, given that the chain begins with a partition decree and a notarial deed of gift subject to a reserved life interest and then runs through three successive intestacies.
gold_answer_draft.rule: The intestacy links are governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance: s.21(1) makes the Ordinance the governing law for intestate succession to immovable property in Sri Lanka; s.20 confines Part III to estates of persons dying after its proclamation; s.22 gives a surviving spouse one-half; s.23 sets the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals; s.24 gives children a preferent right per capita; s.25 divides the estate between a sole surviving parent and the siblings; s.26 passes the estate to siblings of whole or half blood when both parents have failed; s.27 and s.29 govern the half-blood division; and s.30 requires per capita division among heirs equally near in degree. The two earlier links are not covered: the Ordinance is silent on the effect of a reserved life interest and, by s.36, remits such questions to Roman-Dutch common law, and the Partition Law is not part of this corpus.
gold_answer_draft.application: On the statutory material the chain from Kapila onwards can be stated. Kapila died intestate on 24 January 2011 leaving his widow Champa and four children Anusha, Prema, Rupa and Seetha, so Champa took one-half under s.22 and each child 1/8 under s.24. Anusha died issueless on 15 June 2012 leaving her husband Hasitha Perera, who took 1/16 under s.22, the balance passing to her three half-sisters on the father's side under s.26 read with s.29 and s.30. Prema died unmarried and issueless on 4 September 2015, her surviving mother Champa taking half of her share and her full sisters Rupa and Seetha the other half under s.25. The two earlier links of the pedigree, the vesting of Lot 1 in Mahesh under the Final Decree and the passing of dominium to Kapila under Deed of Gift No 925 with the life interest determining on the donor's death in 2008, cannot be supported from any provision in this corpus.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree cannot be completed on statutory authority alone. The succession portion is fully supported by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance and yields Champa, Rupa, Seetha and Hasitha Perera as the present owners, but the first two links of the devolution rest on the Partition Law, which is absent from the corpus, and on the Roman-Dutch law of donations and life interests to which s.36 of the Ordinance itself defers. The question is therefore reserved for a source of authority beyond this corpus.

Every step of that computation, the widow's half, the children's per capita half, the devolution of a childless intestate's share to spouse and collaterals, the half-blood rule and the surviving parent's half, is supplied by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance. No judicial authority or non-statutory doctrine is needed to fix the fractions.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What fractional shares in Lot 1 are presently held by each heir, after the intestate deaths of Kapila on 24 January 2011, of Anusha on 15 June 2012 and of Prema on 4 September 2015.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Intestate succession to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (s.21(1)), which applies to the estate of any person dying after its proclamation (s.20). A surviving spouse first takes one-half of the intestate's property (s.22). Subject to that, inheritance passes in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals (s.23), children taking equally per capita and the issue of a deceased child taking per stirpes (s.24). If descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters, together with half-brothers and sisters related through the deceased parent, take the other half (s.25). If both parents have failed, the estate goes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood (s.26); where all the half-siblings are related on one side only they take the whole, unless an ascendant on the other side survives (s.29). Heirs equally near in degree take per capita (s.30). The word 'unmarried' means not having a husband or wife living (s.3).
gold_answer_draft.application: Kapila held the entirety of Lot 1 under Deed of Gift No 925 once his father's reserved life interest ended on Mahesh's death on 24 April 2008. On Kapila's intestate death on 24 January 2011 his widow Champa took one-half (s.22) and his four surviving children Anusha, Prema, Rupa and Seetha took the remaining half equally per capita under s.24, that is 1/8 each. Anusha died on 15 June 2012 issueless, leaving her husband Hasitha Perera, who took one-half of her 1/8, that is 1/16 (s.22). Her descendants having failed and both her parents Kapila and Sandya having predeceased her, the balance 1/16 passed to her siblings under s.26; her only siblings were the three half-sisters Prema, Rupa and Seetha, all related to her on her father's side alone, and no ascendant on her mother's side is shown to survive, so under s.29 they took the whole 1/16, per capita under s.30, that is 1/48 each. Each of Prema, Rupa and Seetha then held 1/8 + 1/48 = 7/48. Prema died on 4 September 2015 unmarried (s.3) and issueless, so no spouse's half is deducted under s.22 and no descendant takes under s.24. Her father Kapila had predeceased her and her mother Champa survived, so under s.25 Champa took half of 7/48, that is 7/96, and the other 7/96 went to her sisters. Her only surviving siblings were her full sisters Rupa and Seetha, Anusha having already died issueless, so they took 7/192 each under s.25 read with s.30. Section 27 does not alter Anusha's devolution because she left no full siblings, so the half-blood division there is governed by s.29.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The present shares in Lot 1 are: Champa Gunesekera 55/96 (that is 110/192), being 1/2 inherited from Kapila plus 7/96 inherited from Prema; Rupa Gunesekera 35/192; Seetha Gunesekera 35/192; and Hasitha Perera 12/192, that is 1/16, as the widower of Anusha. These fractions total 192/192. The computation assumes, as the facts do not state otherwise, that Anusha and Prema each died intestate and that no ascendant on Sandya's side survived Anusha. Malani and Mithila take nothing in this land because Mahesh had already gifted the entirety away in 2006.

answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate succession to the immovable property Lot 1 is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, which applies to the estate of any person dying after its proclamation.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person who dies intestate.
Subject to the spouse's half, children are preferent to all others and take equally per capita, the issue of a deceased child taking by representation.
Where descendants fail and both parents have predeceased the intestate, the estate passes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood, and their issue by representation.
Where all the surviving half-siblings are related to the intestate on one side only, they take the whole inheritance unless a grandparent or higher ascendant related on the other side survives.

Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters, together with half-siblings related through the deceased parent, take the other half.
Heirs who are equally near in degree to the intestate take per capita and not per stirpes.
A person who dies unmarried leaves no husband or wife living, so no spouse's half falls to be deducted from that estate.
On Kapila's intestate death on 24 January 2011 his widow Champa took one-half of Lot 1 and his four surviving children Anusha, Prema, Rupa and Seetha took 1/8 each.
Anusha's husband Hasitha Perera took one-half of her 1/8 share, that is 1/16.

The balance 1/16 of Anusha's share passed to her three half-sisters Prema, Rupa and Seetha, who took 1/48 each, both her parents having predeceased her and all her siblings being related to her on her father's side only.
After Anusha's death each of Prema, Rupa and Seetha held 7/48 of Lot 1.
On Prema's death unmarried and issueless on 4 September 2015 her surviving mother Champa took half of her 7/48, that is 7/96, and her full sisters Rupa and Seetha took 7/192 each.
The present shares are Champa 55/96, Rupa 35/192, Seetha 35/192 and Hasitha Perera 1/16.
Malani and Mithila hold no share in Lot 1, because Mahesh had gifted the entirety to Kapila before his death.
